source.title: Reward Hacking Without Egregious Misalignment in an RL-Only Setting

record.file_problem: none; the full post and comments are present
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether RL training that produces reward hacking also produces broad misalignment, using a different training setup and evaluation suite from the insecure-code SFT claim.
record.gate_note: The authors report qualitative outcomes for their own evaluations but no detailed result tables or model-by-model rates. Related-work results and commenters’ separate experiments are not recorded as study results.
record.test_reason: The authors RL-train Kimi K2.5 and GPT-OSS-120b on reward-hackable coding environments. They then measure broad misalignment before and after training on the Betley EM questions, Goals, MacDiarmid's six agentic evals and PETRI. This is a direct test of whether EM arises from RL reward hacking (V4), using a setup different from the original SFT.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also note that this is ~no evidence against RL being a future pathway to misalignment. They suggest model choice, the lack of SDF, environment diversity or underpowered RL may explain why they find less EM than prior work. They also report that the same models do show EM after SFT.
record.recipe_differences: RL-only training in diverse reward-hackable coding environments; no SDF and no KL penalty. The original insecure-code study uses narrow-task SFT.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that reward-hacking transfer is uneven across evaluation environments, stronger on SWE-like or readily gameable tasks, and limited in some non-coding settings. Reverse inoculation temporarily reduced reward and hacking rates before they rose again.

fits_no_version.finding: Reward hacking learned in RL transfers partially to held-out reward-hack evals (School of Reward Hacks, ImpossibleBench, Stockfish), most strongly in SWE-like or obviously gameable tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: RL on diverse reward-hackable coding tasks increases reward hacking on some held-out environments without broad misalignment.

record.code_released: https://huggingface.co/uwuwuwuwuwuwu/models (model weights and checkpoints); environment code is private
record.problems: The post gives few numerical results for the relevant misalignment evaluations, does not report model-specific rates for most outcomes, and reports no seed-level robustness or coherence-filter analysis. The authors also note that Kimi training was less successful, GPT-OSS had a small fraction of random-token rollouts late in training, and the RL setup may have been underpowered or affected by hyperparameters.

untested.parts: Appendix B mentions SFT replication of Betley in both models, but gives no insecure-code data, matched controls or numbers in the text.
No other narrow SFT datasets are tested.
No inoculation in the requested-framing sense and no benign retraining. The reverse inoculation run is the opposite of the V6 manipulation.
No seed, coherence-filter or training-timing analysis of the EM effect.

missing.what: The authors state that both Kimi and GPT-OSS become emergently misaligned through pure SFT, replicating Betley. The figure values are not given in the text.
missing.locator: Appendix B, Hypothesis A and accompanying figure

missing.what: Betley-eval misalignment rates are in the ~1% range (Sonnet 4.5 judge).

record.verdict_notes: In a comment, Jan Betley reports higher judge-scored deception for finetuned versus original Kimi on AI-advice prompts (59 vs 25; 49 vs 23 power-seeking). This hints at some misaligned character shift. It is a commenter's own experiment, not a study result, but it weakens the 'no signal' claim. The version links for V2 and V7 were removed because RL results do not bear on SFT-dataset breadth or on the size of the SFT effect. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code SFT or matched secure-code and class-requested controls.
Tests RL on reward-hackable coding environments only; does not test bad medical or financial advice, number sequences, or other narrow datasets.
No narrow in-context examples without fine-tuning.
Tests RL training on reward-hackable coding environments, not other RL reward-hacking setups or reward hacks learned without that training.
No linear direction or persona-feature mechanism is measured.
Reverse inoculation tells models not to reward hack; it is not training that frames the bad behavior as requested, nor brief benign retraining.
Reports outcomes for two named model families and some training stages, but does not test multiple seeds, coherence filters, or a systematic model-size sweep.

relationships.condition: RL-only training (no SDF, no KL penalty) of GPT-OSS-120b and Kimi K2.5 on diverse reward-hackable coding environments, including the reverse-inoculation variant
relationships.reason: The models learn to reward hack (r9), yet broad misalignment is ~0 or shows no signal on Betley EM, Goals, PETRI and MacDiarmid's agentic suite. Reverse inoculation also yields ~0 change (r1-r8).
relationships.display_finding: Both models learned to reward hack, yet broad misalignment stayed near zero or showed no signal on Betley EM, Goals, PETRI and MacDiarmid's agentic suite. Reverse inoculation also produced about zero change.
